description: Background detection engine that identifies recurring charges from transaction history, tracks price changes, projects a forward-looking bill calendar, and splits budget spending into committed (recurring) vs discretionary. Runs silently after every Plaid sync — no interactive prompts.

timing.gatingCondition: Requires stable transaction history with 3+ months of data for reliable frequency detection. Budget calculator and anomaly detector patterns are the architectural templates.

principles: Background-first: detection runs silently after sync, never interrupts the user with 'is this recurring?' prompts
Conservative classification: 3+ occurrences required for monthly patterns, 2+ for quarterly/annual — false negatives are acceptable, false positives are not
Merchant normalization must be aggressive but reversible — group 'NETFLIX.COM/1234' with 'NETFLIX.COM/5678' but preserve original names for display
Idempotent: re-running detection updates existing records, never duplicates. Same pattern as transfer detection and anomaly detection
Amount tolerance handles real-world variance (tax, tips, plan changes) without losing the signal
This feature is the data foundation for Feature 20 (Cash Flow Forecasting) — the recurring_expenses table is the source of truth for known future obligations
SECRETS INVARIANT: recurring expense data surfaces merchant names and amounts only — no account numbers, tokens, or PII in API responses or LLM context

techStack.database: PostgreSQL — new recurring_expenses and recurring_expense_history tables
techStack.charting: Chart.js 4.x for bill calendar timeline visualization (optional, stretch)
techStack.testing: node:test for detection engine, normalization, frequency classification, and API coverage

userStories.title: Merchant name normalization
acceptanceCriteria: Normalize merchant_name by: lowercase, strip trailing numeric IDs (6+ digits), strip date patterns (MM/DD, YYYY), strip common suffixes (LLC, INC, CO), collapse whitespace
Preserve original merchant_name for display — normalization is for grouping only
Handle null merchant_name gracefully (fall back to transaction name field)
Normalization is deterministic — same input always produces same key
Edge cases: empty string, unicode, very long names, names that are entirely numeric
userStories.testStrategy: node:test unit tests with 30+ fixture merchant names covering real Plaid data patterns (Netflix, Spotify, insurance companies, utilities, mortgage servicers, property tax). Test normalization key stability across runs.

userStories.title: Recurring pattern detection engine
acceptanceCriteria: Group non-transfer, non-pending transactions by normalized merchant key
For each group with 2+ transactions, compute median interval between consecutive dates
Classify frequency: weekly (5-9 days), biweekly (12-16 days), monthly (27-34 days), quarterly (85-100 days), semi-annual (170-195 days), annual (350-380 days)
Require minimum occurrences: 3 for weekly/biweekly/monthly, 2 for quarterly/semi-annual/annual
Amount clustering: group transactions within ±10% of median amount (configurable via recurring_amount_tolerance_pct)
Confidence scoring: high (consistent interval ≤15% CV + consistent amount ≤10% CV), medium (interval or amount varies but not both), low (sparse data or high variance)
Upsert into recurring_expenses table on (account_id, merchant_key, frequency)
Mark items not seen in 2× expected interval as status='stale'
Mark items not seen in 4× expected interval as status='likely_cancelled'
Skip transactions older than recurring_lookback_months (default 18) config setting
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with fixture transaction sets: monthly subscription (12 charges, consistent), quarterly insurance (4 charges), annual renewal (2 charges), price-changing subscription (amount drift), cancelled subscription (stopped 3 months ago), false positive (3 Amazon purchases that aren't recurring). Test frequency classification, confidence scoring, stale detection.

userStories.title: Price change tracking
acceptanceCriteria: Each detection run inserts a row into recurring_expense_history with (recurring_expense_id, amount, transaction_date)
Only insert if the latest transaction is newer than the most recent history entry
Price change flagged when latest amount differs from prior amount by >$1.00 AND >5%
recurring_expenses table stores latest_amount, prior_amount, price_change_pct, price_change_date
Price increases get price_change_direction='up', decreases get 'down'
History is append-only — never modified or deleted
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: price change detection with fixture history (stable price, gradual increase, sudden jump, decrease). Verify threshold logic (below $1 or 5% not flagged). Verify history append-only behavior.

userStories.title: Bill calendar projection
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/recurring/calendar?days=30 returns expected charges in the next N days (default 30, max 90)
Each entry: merchant_name, expected_amount, expected_date, account_name, frequency, confidence
Expected date computed from last_seen_date + frequency interval
Only active recurring items with confidence >= medium included
Items with status='stale' or 'likely_cancelled' excluded
Results sorted by expected_date ascending
Endpoint requires authentication (any member)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: projection accuracy for monthly (last seen March 5 → expect April 5), quarterly (last seen Jan 15 → expect April 15), edge cases (month boundary, leap year). Auth guard test.

userStories.title: Recurring expenses API endpoints
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/recurring returns all detected recurring expenses with latest amount, frequency, confidence, status, price change info
GET /api/recurring/summary returns committed monthly total, count of active items, count of price increases, count of stale items
GET /api/recurring/:id/history returns amount history for a single recurring item
PATCH /api/recurring/:id allows parent to update status (active/paused/ignored) or override frequency
All endpoints require authentication; PATCH requires parent role
Response excludes account IDs and raw transaction IDs — only display-safe fields
userStories.testStrategy: node:test integration tests for all endpoints: response shapes, auth guards, parent-only writes, status transitions, history ordering.

userStories.title: Post-sync detection hook
acceptanceCriteria: After each Plaid sync completes (both 6 AM and 8 PM), recurring detection runs automatically
Detection runs after transfer detection but before anomaly detection in the sync pipeline
Detection errors are logged but do not fail the sync
First run on deployment performs a full historical scan (slower, one-time)
Subsequent runs are incremental: only re-evaluate merchants with new transactions since last run
Last detection timestamp stored in app_config as recurring_last_detection_at
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: verify detection is called after sync. Verify incremental mode skips unchanged merchants. Verify error isolation (detection failure doesn't fail sync).

userStories.title: Recurring expenses page (frontend)
acceptanceCriteria: New page: recurring.html accessible from nav as 'Recurring'
Nav entry added between Budget and Reports
Three sections: Active Recurring (sorted by amount desc), Bill Calendar (next 30 days), Stale/Cancelled
Each recurring item shows: merchant name, amount, frequency badge, next expected date, account name, confidence indicator, price change badge if applicable
Price change badge: red up-arrow with dollar and percentage delta for increases
Bill calendar: timeline or list view of upcoming charges with running total
Stale section: items not seen recently, with 'last seen' date and suggested action
Responsive: card layout on mobile, table on desktop
Parent can click item to see amount history and toggle status (active/paused/ignored)
Loading state while data fetches, empty state if no recurring items detected yet
userStories.testStrategy: Playwright e2e: page loads, recurring items render, bill calendar section present. Manual: verify against known subscriptions, price change badges, mobile layout.

userStories.title: Committed vs discretionary budget integration
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/budget response gains two new fields: committed_total (sum of active monthly-equivalent recurring amounts) and discretionary_total (total_budgeted - committed_total)
Budget page shows committed vs discretionary bar or summary line above category cards
Dashboard summary hero gains a committed/discretionary line: '$3,400 committed · $1,700 discretionary'
Monthly-equivalent conversion: weekly ×4.33, biweekly ×2.17, quarterly ÷3, semi-annual ÷6, annual ÷12
Only 'active' recurring items with confidence >= medium count toward committed total
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: monthly-equivalent conversions for all frequency types. Verify committed total excludes stale/ignored items. Integration test for budget summary response shape.

userStories.title: LLM context enrichment with recurring data
acceptanceCriteria: context-assembler adds recurring summary to weekly, monthly, and query contexts
Context includes: committed_monthly_total, count_active, top 5 recurring by amount, any price changes this month, any upcoming annual renewals in next 60 days
Weekly digest LLM prompt can now reference 'Your $3,400 in committed monthly charges include...'
What-if scenarios gain recurring expense context for more accurate projections
All recurring context passes through sanitizeForLLM
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: verify recurring context structure, verify sanitization, verify empty state when no recurring items exist.

high: Merchant name normalization quality determines detection accuracy. Mitigation: start conservative (exact lowercased match), iterate normalization rules based on real Plaid merchant data. Ship a manual override escape hatch (PATCH status) for false positives.
medium: Insufficient transaction history on first run — new Plaid connections may have <3 months. Mitigation: Monarch import data (source='imported') counts toward history; detection gracefully handles sparse data with lower confidence scores.

Amount variance on recurring charges (taxes, tips, plan tier changes) may prevent clustering. Mitigation: configurable tolerance (default ±10%), and frequency detection weighs interval consistency more than amount consistency.
low: Detection post-sync adds processing time. Mitigation: incremental mode only re-evaluates merchants with new transactions. Full scan is one-time on deployment.
Nav bar getting crowded with another entry. Mitigation: Recurring fits naturally between Budget and Reports as a peer financial view.
